history.dynasty: Travancore; the idol is said to have been worshipped by a soldier of the Travancore army (Nair Brigade) at Padmanabhapuram and installed at Pazhavangadi when the capital shifted to Thiruvananthapuram
history.period: Installed at the present site in 1795 AD (one source credits construction to Maharaja Ayilyam Thirunal and a renovation in 1860); since the integration of the Travancore forces, the temple has been maintained by the Indian Army
history.summary: The Pazhavangadi Ganapathy Temple at East Fort, adjoining the Padmanabhaswamy Temple, is one of Kerala's most popular Ganesha shrines. Its origin legend: a Travancore army soldier on night guard duty at Padmanabhapuram, harassed by a Yakshi, found a small Ganesha idol on a riverbed and carried it for protection; when the capital moved to Thiruvananthapuram in 1795, the garrison shifted and installed the idol at Pazhavangadi - literally 'Pazha Angadi' (fruit market), the old market at the site. The temple is maintained by the Indian Army, rare among Kerala temples. The main idol sits with the right leg folded; the complex also displays 32 forms of Ganesha, a gold idol alongside a granite one, and a reclining Vishnu on Anantha said to be made of kudusarkara, herbs and salagramam. The signature offering is coconut-breaking - over 2,500 coconuts a day - believed to remove obstacles and fulfil wishes. Strict dress code applies for men entering the sanctum.

name: Pazhavangadi Ganapathy Temple
town_description: Thiruvananthapuram (Trivandrum) is the capital of Kerala, a coastal city built on seven hills at the state's southwestern tip. It is a historic administrative and cultural centre - seat of the Travancore royal family, major museums, the Kerala legislature, and the Technopark IT hub - as well as a beach destination (Kovalam, Varkala nearby). The East Fort quarter is the old temple district of the Travancore capital, housing the Padmanabhaswamy Temple, the Pazhavangadi Ganapathy Temple and the bustling Chalai bazaar.

travel.road: At East Fort on Padmavilasam Road; city buses and autos to East Fort bus stand
